content:
According to reports, Apple has been collaborating with LG to develop a "second-party" Home accessory, but the latest leaked information shows that another company will also launch "second-party" smart home products.

iOS 27.2 code reveals that the new Home accessories will appear as "second-party," not manufactured by LG.

Over the past day, multiple pieces of information have leaked, revealing Apple's ambitions to expand its smart home ecosystem.

In addition to a series of its own Home products expected to debut next week, including the next-generation Apple TV 4K, the "HomePad," and the HomePod mini 2, the company is reportedly also collaborating with LG to develop several new home accessories.

These accessories are co-developed by Apple and LG, but will be sold under the LG brand. Images leaked today reveal their appearance:

  • Leaked images show Apple-designed smart door locks, thermostats, and other LG products
  • Apple's new Home camera and doorbell with LG appear in leaked images

It makes sense for Apple to strengthen its smart home ecosystem through co-developed products. In fact, similar partnerships may not be limited to LG alone.

Leaker pdfu discovered two additional Home accessories in iOS 27.2, also labeled as "second-party" products.

These two accessories are a smart thermostat under the Schneider brand, and a temperature and humidity sensor.

According to pdfu's article, currently in Apple's HomeKit database, only the new batch of LG accessories and these two Schneider products carry the "second-party" label.

Accessories classified as second-party will receive "special treatment" from the operating system.

It is not yet known whether Apple's collaboration with Schneider is as close as the one with LG, but the code does hint at this possibility.

What are your thoughts on Apple's reportedly new Home product strategy? Feel free to share your opinions in the comments section.
